newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada April trade surplus shrinks to C$1.72 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada April trade surplus shrinks to C$1.72 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus narrowed in April to C$1.72 billion from C$2.60 billion in March (revised from C$3.12 billion), Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
The agency said overall imports hit a record high in April, as did imports and exports with the United States.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.9 billion in April, with exports of C$23.9 billion and imports of C$20.6 billion.

Statistics Canada said overall imports at C$22.88 billion broke a record high set earlier in January 1997 at C$21.95 billion. Exports to the United States at C$20.01 billion also broke January's record of C$19.93 billion, while imports to the United States at C$17.14 billion in April broke a record set in February 1997 at C$16.68 billion.

StatsCan said that strong import growth combined with steady exports pulled down the trade surplus in April. Surpluses with the United States and Japan declined and deficits increased with all other trading partners.
The federal agency said all import sectors posted gains in April, the largest being for machinery, energy products and auto parts.
Although more goods were imported from all major trading partners except Japan, shipments from the United States contributed the most to the month's increase, StatsCan said.

Exports saw little change for the third consecutive month in April, rising 0.3 percent. StatsCan said that although shipments of machinery edged up, moderately lower exports for most other sectors offset most of the gain.
The federal agency said increased exports to the United States and the European Union were all but overshadowed by reduced shipments to all other trading partners.
